text:
Priya S: FYI customer (acct redacted) seeing intermittent 500s + high tail latency on generation endpoints since ~2026-03-15T18:12Z. They attached 3 request IDs: rq_3a2f9, rq_3a2fb, rq_3a2ff. Asking for minimal repro snippets (curl / py / js / go) and a debug bundle upload path so they can share logs.

Alex C: Can you paste one full curl with the headers they used and the exact timestamps for those request IDs? Also which SDK version are they on?

Priya S: They were using our hosted API (prod-west), SDK unknown initially. Timestamp window for rq_3a2f9 ~ 2026-03-15T18:12:07Z. Customer provided this quick curl they ran:

```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-xyz","input":"summarize: keep short","max_tokens":128}'
```

Priya S: They asked for tiny language examples; I prepared minimal repro snippets they can try to run and attach results. Please review before I send: 

Python (requests):
```python
import requests
url = "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate"
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer REPLACE_ME", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
data = {"model": "gpt-xyz", "input": "test latency repro", "max_tokens": 32}
resp = requests.post(url, json=data, headers=headers, timeout=15)
print(resp.status_code, resp.text)
```

Node (fetch):
```js
const fetch = require('node-fetch')
fetch('https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer REPLACE_ME', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'gpt-xyz', input: 'test latency repro', max_tokens: 32 }),
  timeout: 15000
}).then(r => r.text()).then(console.log).catch(console.error)
```

Go (net/http):
```go
package main
import (
  "bytes"
  "fmt"
  "io/ioutil"
  "net/http"
  "time"
)
func main() {
  client := &http.Client{Timeout: 15 * time.Second}
  body := []byte(`{"model":"gpt-xyz","input":"test latency repro","max_tokens":32}`)
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate", bytes.NewBuffer(body))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer REPLACE_ME")
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
  if err != nil { fmt.Println("err:", err); return }
  b, _ := ioutil.ReadAll(resp.Body)
  fmt.Println(resp.StatusCode, string(b))
}
```

Priya S: I also suggested they include the `X-Request-ID` header we return in responses (or the request IDs above) and the exact wallclock times. Told them to collect the response headers when they hit 500s.

Morgan P: Good. Ask them to run the curl with `-i` to capture response headers and `--trace-ascii /tmp/curl.trace` if they can. Also request `system` info: region, whether they were on our private/dedicated pool, and SDK version.

Samir R: If they can reproduce, request they run one short trace with `strace -f -e trace=network` (linux) or equivalent and attach. Also we'll need the debug bundle; send them the secure upload link: https://uploads.redwood-inference.com/put/debug-bundles (pre-provisioned, TTL 72h).

oncall-bot: Incident ticket created: #INC-2026-0457 (linked to support ticket).

Alex C: Quick ask — include the exact server time they saw the 500s and the request latency from their side (curl `-w "%{time_total}\n"`). If they used our SDKs, capture `rdw_client_version`/`package.json`/`go.mod`.

Priya S: Will send customer the revised repro kit + upload link. I'll ask them to run the exact curl above with `-i -w` and attach both stdout and the curl.trace. I'll also include the three tiny SDK snippets so they can try all three runtimes and paste back the outputs for those request IDs.

Morgan P: Once they upload, tag @eng-sre and paste the upload URL + request IDs in the ticket. We'll pull traces and check kernel-level drops / NAT timeouts.

Samir R: If we can't repro within 24h, escalate to infra oncall for packet capture on the egress nodes that served those request IDs.

Priya S: Sending now. Thanks all — I'll post back when they upload. :thumbsup:
